claim: Bcl11b has been linked to neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric disorders associated with synaptic dysfunction.
source: The transcription factor Bcl11b has been linked to neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric disorders associated with synaptic dysfunction.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature in the introduction section.

claim: Bcl11b is highly expressed in dentate gyrus granule neurons.
source: Bcl11b is highly expressed in dentate gyrus granule neurons and is required for the structural and functional integrity of mossy fiber-CA3 synapses.
evidence: This is supported by references to prior work and confirmed by immunohistochemistry data shown in the manuscript.

claim: Bcl11b is required for the structural and functional integrity of mossy fiber-CA3 synapses.
source: Bcl11b is highly expressed in dentate gyrus granule neurons and is required for the structural and functional integrity of mossy fiber-CA3 synapses.
evidence: This is supported by prior published work and experimental data in this manuscript.

claim: C1ql2 is a direct functional target of Bcl11b.
source: We show in mice that the synaptic organizer molecule C1ql2 is a direct functional target of Bcl11b that regulates synaptic vesicle recruitment and long-term potentiation at mossy fiber-CA3 synapses in vivo and in vitro.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data including transcriptomic analysis, ChIP, and rescue experiments presented in the manuscript.

claim: C1ql2 regulates synaptic vesicle recruitment at mossy fiber-CA3 synapses in vivo and in vitro.
source: We show in mice that the synaptic organizer molecule C1ql2 is a direct functional target of Bcl11b that regulates synaptic vesicle recruitment and long-term potentiation at mossy fiber-CA3 synapses in vivo and in vitro.
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data showing changes in synaptic vesicle distribution and docking in C1ql2 knockdown and rescue experiments.

claim: C1ql2 regulates long-term potentiation at mossy fiber-CA3 synapses in vivo and in vitro.
source: We show in mice that the synaptic organizer molecule C1ql2 is a direct functional target of Bcl11b that regulates synaptic vesicle recruitment and long-term potentiation at mossy fiber-CA3 synapses in vivo and in vitro.
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological recordings showing rescue of LTP upon C1ql2 reintroduction and loss of LTP upon C1ql2 knockdown.

claim: C1ql2 exerts its functions through direct interaction with Nrxn3(25b+).
source: Furthermore, we demonstrate C1ql2 to exert its functions through direct interaction with a specific splice variant of neurexin-3, Nrxn3(25b+).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro co-culture experiments, mutant C1ql2 experiments, and Nrxn3 deletion experiments.

claim: Interruption of C1ql2-Nrxn3(25b+) interaction by expression of a non-binding C1ql2 mutant recapitulates major parts of the Bcl11b mutant phenotype.
source: Interruption of C1ql2-Nrxn3(25b+) interaction by expression of a non-binding C1ql2 mutant or by deletion of Nrxn3 in the dentate gyrus granule neurons recapitulates major parts of the Bcl11b as well as C1ql2 mutant phenotype.
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data showing impaired synaptic vesicle recruitment in C1ql2.K262E rescue experiments.

claim: Deletion of Nrxn3 in dentate gyrus granule neurons recapitulates major parts of the Bcl11b mutant phenotype.
source: Interruption of C1ql2-Nrxn3(25b+) interaction by expression of a non-binding C1ql2 mutant or by deletion of Nrxn3 in the dentate gyrus granule neurons recapitulates major parts of the Bcl11b as well as C1ql2 mutant phenotype.
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data showing impaired synaptic vesicle recruitment in Nrxn conditional triple knockout experiments.

claim: Disruptions in synaptic structure and function have been identified as a major determinant in the manifestation of various neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric disorders.
source: Disruptions in synaptic structure and function have been identified as a major determinant in the manifestation of various neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric disorders, such as autism spectrum disorder, schizophrenia, and intellectual disability (Hayashi-Takagi, 2017; Lepeta et al., 2016; Zoghbi and Bear, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Cell adhesion molecules at both the pre- and post-synaptic side act as synaptic organizers whose unique combination determines the structural and functional properties of the synapse.
source: These mechanisms involve cell adhesion molecules at both the pre- and post-synaptic side that act as synaptic organizers, whose unique combination determines the structural and functional properties of the synapse.
evidence: This is based on established scientific knowledge and supported by citations.

claim: Genes encoding for several known synaptic proteins have been implicated in neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric disorders.
source: Furthermore, recent advances in the genetics of neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric disorders have implicated genes encoding for several of the known synaptic proteins, supporting a role for these molecules in the pathogenesis of corresponding disorders (Südhof, 2021; Torres et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The functional specification of the synapse is sensitive to the combination of distinct synaptic proteins and their relative expression levels.
source: The sensitivity of the functional specification of the synapse to the combination of distinct synaptic proteins and their relative expression levels suggests that genetically encoded programs define at least facets of the synaptic properties in a cell-type-specific manner (Südhof, 2017).
evidence: This is based on inference from cited literature and established knowledge.

claim: Genetically encoded programs define at least facets of the synaptic properties in a cell-type-specific manner.
source: The sensitivity of the functional specification of the synapse to the combination of distinct synaptic proteins and their relative expression levels suggests that genetically encoded programs define at least facets of the synaptic properties in a cell-type-specific manner (Südhof, 2017).
evidence: This is an inference supported by cited literature.

claim: Several synaptic proteins promote formation of functional pre- and postsynaptic assemblies when presented in non-neuronal cells.
source: Several of the synaptic proteins have been shown to promote formation of functional pre- and postsynaptic assemblies when presented in non-neuronal cells (Dalva et al., 2000; Dean et al., 2003; Scheiffele et al., 2000), showing that their ability to specify synapses is in part independent of signaling processes and neuronal activity and supporting the idea that synaptic function is governed by cues linked to cellular origin (Gomez et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The ability of synaptic proteins to specify synapses is in part independent of signaling processes and neuronal activity.
source: Several of the synaptic proteins have been shown to promote formation of functional pre- and postsynaptic assemblies when presented in non-neuronal cells (Dalva et al., 2000; Dean et al., 2003; Scheiffele et al., 2000), showing that their ability to specify synapses is in part independent of signaling processes and neuronal activity and supporting the idea that synaptic function is governed by cues linked to cellular origin (Gomez et al., 2021).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from cited experimental evidence.

claim: Bcl11b has been implicated in various disorders of the nervous system including Alzheimer's and Huntington's disease, and schizophrenia.
source: Bcl11b (also known as Ctip2) is a zinc finger transcription factor that has been implicated in various disorders of the nervous system including Alzheimer's and Huntington's disease, and schizophrenia (Kunkle et al., 2016; Song et al., 2022; Whitton et al., 2018; Whitton et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Patients with BCL11B mutations present with neurodevelopmental delay, overall learning deficits as well as impaired speech acquisition and autistic features.
source: Patients with BCL11B mutations present with neurodevelopmental delay, overall learning deficits as well as impaired speech acquisition and autistic features (Eto et al., 2022; Lessel et al., 2018; Punwani et al., 2016; Yang et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Bcl11b is expressed in several neuron types, including the dentate gyrus granule neurons of the hippocampus.
source: Bcl11b is expressed in several neuron types, including the dentate gyrus granule neurons (DGN) of the hippocampus.
evidence: This is supported by citations and immunohistochemistry data in the manuscript.

claim: Expression of Bcl11b in the DGN starts during embryonic development and persists into adulthood.
source: Expression of Bcl11b in the DGN starts during embryonic development and persists into adulthood (Simon et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Bcl11b plays a crucial role in the development of the hippocampal mossy fiber system.
source: We have previously demonstrated that Bcl11b plays a crucial role in the development of the hippocampal mossy fiber system, adult hippocampal neurogenesis as well as hippocampal learning and memory (Simon et al., 2016; Simon et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: Bcl11b plays a crucial role in adult hippocampal neurogenesis.
source: We have previously demonstrated that Bcl11b plays a crucial role in the development of the hippocampal mossy fiber system, adult hippocampal neurogenesis as well as hippocampal learning and memory (Simon et al., 2016; Simon et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: Bcl11b plays a crucial role in hippocampal learning and memory.
source: We have previously demonstrated that Bcl11b plays a crucial role in the development of the hippocampal mossy fiber system, adult hippocampal neurogenesis as well as hippocampal learning and memory (Simon et al., 2016; Simon et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: In the mature hippocampus, Bcl11b is critical for the structural and functional integrity of mossy fiber synapses.
source: In the mature hippocampus, Bcl11b is critical for the structural and functional integrity of mossy fiber synapses (MFS), the connections between DGN and CA3 pyramidal neurons (De Bruyckere et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior published work.

claim: MFS have a critical role in learning and memory stemming from their unique structural and functional properties.
source: MFS have a critical role in learning and memory stemming from their unique structural and functional properties, such as an enormous pool of releasable synaptic vesicles (SV), and reliable presynaptic short- and long-term plasticity (Nicoll and Schmitz, 2005; Rollenhagen and Lübke, 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: MFS have an enormous pool of releasable synaptic vesicles.
source: MFS have a critical role in learning and memory stemming from their unique structural and functional properties, such as an enormous pool of releasable synaptic vesicles (SV), and reliable presynaptic short- and long-term plasticity (Nicoll and Schmitz, 2005; Rollenhagen and Lübke, 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: MFS have reliable presynaptic short- and long-term plasticity.
source: MFS have a critical role in learning and memory stemming from their unique structural and functional properties, such as an enormous pool of releasable synaptic vesicles (SV), and reliable presynaptic short- and long-term plasticity (Nicoll and Schmitz, 2005; Rollenhagen and Lübke, 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Conditional ablation of Bcl11b in murine DGN impairs presynaptic recruitment of SV.
source: Conditional ablation of Bcl11b in murine DGN impairs presynaptic recruitment of SV and abolishes mossy fiber long-term potentiation (MF-LTP; De Bruyckere et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior published work.

claim: Conditional ablation of Bcl11b in murine DGN abolishes mossy fiber long-term potentiation.
source: Conditional ablation of Bcl11b in murine DGN impairs presynaptic recruitment of SV and abolishes mossy fiber long-term potentiation (MF-LTP; De Bruyckere et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior published work.

claim: C1ql2 is a member of the C1q-like protein family.
source: In the present study, we show that the secreted synaptic organizer molecule C1ql2, a member of the C1q-like protein family (Yuzaki, 2017), is a functional target of Bcl11b in murine DGN.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Reintroduction of C1ql2 in Bcl11b mutant DGN rescued the localization and docking of SV to the active zone.
source: Reintroduction of C1ql2 in Bcl11b mutant DGN rescued the localization and docking of SV to the active zone (AZ), as well as MF-LTP that was abolished upon Bcl11b ablation.
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Reintroduction of C1ql2 in Bcl11b mutant DGN rescued MF-LTP that was abolished upon Bcl11b ablation.
source: Reintroduction of C1ql2 in Bcl11b mutant DGN rescued the localization and docking of SV to the active zone (AZ), as well as MF-LTP that was abolished upon Bcl11b ablation.
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Knock-down of C1ql2 in wildtype animals recapitulated a major part of the MFS phenotype observed in Bcl11b mutants.
source: Knock-down (KD) of C1ql2 in wildtype animals recapitulated a major part of the MFS phenotype observed in Bcl11b mutants.
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy and electrophysiological data presented in the manuscript.

claim: C1ql2 requires direct interaction with Nrxn3(25b+) to recruit SV in vitro and in vivo.
source: Furthermore, we show that C1ql2 requires direct interaction with a specific neurexin-3 isoform, Nrxn3(25b+), a member of a polymorphic family of presynaptic cell adhesion molecules (Reissner et al., 2013; Südhof, 2017), to recruit SV in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by co-culture experiments, mutant C1ql2 experiments, and Nrxn3 deletion experiments presented in the manuscript.

claim: Localization of C1ql2 along the mossy fiber tract depends on C1ql2-Nrxn3(25b+) interaction.
source: Finally, we observe that localization of C1ql2 along the mossy fiber tract depends on C1ql2-Nrxn3(25b+) interaction.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data showing reduced C1ql2 fluorescence in Nrxn cTKO and C1ql2.K262E rescue experiments.

claim: C1ql2 transcript levels are massively downregulated in Bcl11b mutant DGN.
source: C1ql2 transcript and protein levels are massively downregulated in Bcl11b mutant DGN (Figure 1—figure supplement 1; De Bruyckere et al., 2018), and the Bcl11b protein directly binds to consensus sequences within the C1ql2 promotor (De Bruyckere et al., 2018), suggesting Bcl11b to act on MFS through C1ql2.
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and cited prior work.

claim: C1ql2 protein levels are massively downregulated in Bcl11b mutant DGN.
source: C1ql2 transcript and protein levels are massively downregulated in Bcl11b mutant DGN (Figure 1—figure supplement 1; De Bruyckere et al., 2018), and the Bcl11b protein directly binds to consensus sequences within the C1ql2 promotor (De Bruyckere et al., 2018), suggesting Bcl11b to act on MFS through C1ql2.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and cited prior work.

claim: The Bcl11b protein directly binds to consensus sequences within the C1ql2 promotor.
source: C1ql2 transcript and protein levels are massively downregulated in Bcl11b mutant DGN (Figure 1—figure supplement 1; De Bruyckere et al., 2018), and the Bcl11b protein directly binds to consensus sequences within the C1ql2 promotor (De Bruyckere et al., 2018), suggesting Bcl11b to act on MFS through C1ql2.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior published work.

claim: AAV-mediated re-expression of C1ql2 in the Bcl11b mutant DGN completely restored C1ql2 protein expression.
source: AAV-mediated re-expression of C1ql2 in the Bcl11b mutant DGN completely restored C1ql2 protein expression (Figure 1c–d; Control +EGFP: 1±0.216, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP: 0.2±0.023, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-C1ql2: 2.44±0.745, mean ± SEM).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1c-d.

claim: The spatial distribution of the exogenous C1ql2 protein in mutants was indistinguishable from controls.
source: Furthermore, the spatial distribution of the exogenous C1ql2 protein in mutants was indistinguishable from controls (Figure 1e).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1e.

claim: Exogenous C1ql2 protein precisely localizes at glutamatergic synapses within the stratum lucidum of CA3.
source: Using vGlut1 and Homer1 as pre- and postsynaptic markers, respectively, we observed exogenous C1ql2 protein to precisely localize at glutamatergic synapses within the stratum lucidum (SL) of CA3, confirming that reintroduced C1ql2 is correctly targeted to the MFS (Figure 1f).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1f.

claim: MFS of Bcl11b cKO animals were characterized by a misdistribution of SV in relation to the AZ, with fewer SV being present in the vicinity of AZ.
source: MFS of Bcl11b cKO animals were characterized by a misdistribution of SV in relation to the AZ, with fewer SV being present in the vicinity of AZ, as reflected by a lower average synapse score (Figure 2a–b).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 2a-b.

claim: Reintroduction of C1ql2 fully recovered the synapse score to control values.
source: Reintroduction of C1ql2 fully recovered the synapse score to control values (Figure 2a–b; Control +EGFP: 3.4±0.012, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP: 2.96±0.037, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-C1ql2: 3.47±0.043, mean ± SEM).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 2a-b.

claim: C1ql2 reduced the number of inactive synapses and improved the synapse score of active synapses.
source: As revealed by the relative frequency of the individual synapse scores, C1ql2 not only reduced the number of inactive synapses, characterized by a synapse score of 0, but also improved the synapse score of active synapses (Figure 2c).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: C1ql3 is co-expressed with C1ql2 in DGN.
source: C1ql3, a different member of the C1ql subfamily, is co-expressed with C1ql2 in DGN and the two proteins have been shown to form functional heteromers (Matsuda et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: C1ql2 and C1ql3 have been shown to form functional heteromers.
source: C1ql3, a different member of the C1ql subfamily, is co-expressed with C1ql2 in DGN and the two proteins have been shown to form functional heteromers (Matsuda et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: C1ql3 expression is unchanged in Bcl11b cKO.
source: C1ql3 expression is unchanged in Bcl11b cKO (Figure 2—figure supplement 1a-b; Control +EGFP: 1±0.022, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP: 1.09±0.126, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-C1ql2: 0.87±0.146, mean ± SEM).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry and qPCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1a-b.

claim: Overexpression of C1ql3 in the DGN of Bcl11b cKO neither interfered with C1ql2 expression levels nor was able to rescue the synapse score of Bcl11b mutants.
source: Overexpression of C1ql3 in the DGN of Bcl11b cKO neither interfered with C1ql2 expression levels (Figure 1c–e; Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-C1ql3: 0.29±0.042, mean ± SEM) nor was it able to rescue the synapse score of Bcl11b mutants (Figure 2a–c; Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-C1ql3: 2.97±0.062, mean ± SEM).
evidence: This is supported by western blot and electron microscopy data shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Overexpression of C1ql2 in control animals did not affect the average synapse score.
source: However, this did not affect the average synapse score (Figure 2i–j; Control +EGFP: 3.4±0.012; Control +EGFP-2A-C1ql2: 3.41±0.031; Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-C1ql2: 3.47±0.043, mean ± SEM).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 2i-j.

claim: Bcl11b mutant animals had significantly fewer docked vesicles per 100 nm of AZ profile length compared to control animals.
source: Bcl11b mutant animals had significantly fewer docked vesicles per 100 nm of AZ profile length compared to control animals and more AZ with no docked vesicles at all.
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Rescue of C1ql2 expression restored the number of docked SV to control levels.
source: Rescue of C1ql2 expression restored the number of docked SV to control levels, while the overexpression of C1ql3 did not affect the number of docked vesicles (Figure 2d and f–g; Control +EGFP: 0.53±0.098, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP: 0.24±0.038, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-C1ql2: 0.51±0.049, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-C1ql3: 0.26±0.041, mean ± SEM).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 2d and f-g.

claim: The AZ length remained unchanged in all conditions.
source: The AZ length remained unchanged in all conditions (Figure 2—figure supplement 1c; Control +EGFP: 168.3±4,94, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP: 161.9±5.56, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-C1ql2: 161.91±7.14, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-C1ql3: 171.87±6.74, mean ± SEM).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1c.

claim: Bcl11b and C1ql2 did not affect the size of the docked SV.
source: In contrast to vesicle docking, Bcl11b and C1ql2 did not affect the size of the docked SV (Figure 2e; Control +EGFP: 36.30±1.67, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP: 35.18±1.13, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-C1ql2: 36.35±1.01, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-C1ql3: 36.65±0.1, mean ± SEM).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 2e.

claim: C1ql2 specifically controls SV recruitment downstream of Bcl11b.
source: Thus, our data suggest that C1ql2 specifically controls SV recruitment downstream of Bcl11b.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing rescue of SV recruitment by C1ql2.

claim: Conditional deletion of Bcl11b in the adult hippocampus leads to a loss of MFS.
source: Conditional deletion of Bcl11b in the adult hippocampus also leads to a loss of MFS, as well as reduced ultrastructural complexity of the remaining mossy fiber boutons (MFB; De Bruyckere et al., 2018), posing the question of whether these phenotypic features also depend on C1ql2.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior published work.

claim: Conditional deletion of Bcl11b in the adult hippocampus leads to reduced ultrastructural complexity of the remaining mossy fiber boutons.
source: Conditional deletion of Bcl11b in the adult hippocampus also leads to a loss of MFS, as well as reduced ultrastructural complexity of the remaining mossy fiber boutons (MFB; De Bruyckere et al., 2018), posing the question of whether these phenotypic features also depend on C1ql2.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior published work.

claim: C1ql2 reintroduction in the DGN of Bcl11b cKO did not restore the loss of glutamatergic synapses.
source: Interestingly, C1ql2 reintroduction in the DGN of Bcl11b cKO neither restored the loss of glutamatergic synapses, as quantified by the colocalization of pre- and postsynaptic markers, vGlut1 and Homer1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1d; Control +EGFP: 90.65±8.25, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP: 60.68±4.62, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-C1ql2: 56.84±6.99, mean ± SEM), nor the reduced ultrastructural complexity of MFB, as quantified by the MFB perimeter/area ratio (Figure 2—figure supplement 1e-f; Control +EGFP: 0.0051±0.00031, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP: 0.0042±0.00014, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-C1ql2: 0.0037±0.00021, mean ± SEM).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1d.

claim: C1ql2 reintroduction in the DGN of Bcl11b cKO did not restore the reduced ultrastructural complexity of MFB.
source: Interestingly, C1ql2 reintroduction in the DGN of Bcl11b cKO neither restored the loss of glutamatergic synapses, as quantified by the colocalization of pre- and postsynaptic markers, vGlut1 and Homer1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1d; Control +EGFP: 90.65±8.25, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP: 60.68±4.62, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-C1ql2: 56.84±6.99, mean ± SEM), nor the reduced ultrastructural complexity of MFB, as quantified by the MFB perimeter/area ratio (Figure 2—figure supplement 1e-f; Control +EGFP: 0.0051±0.00031, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP: 0.0042±0.00014, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-C1ql2: 0.0037±0.00021, mean ± SEM).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1e-f.

claim: Bcl11b acts on MFS through C1ql2-dependent as well as -independent signaling pathways.
source: This suggests that Bcl11b acts on MFS through C1ql2-dependent as well as -independent signaling pathways.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that C1ql2 rescues some but not all Bcl11b mutant phenotypes.

claim: Adult-induced Bcl11b cKO results in a loss of MF-LTP.
source: Indeed, adult-induced Bcl11b cKO was previously found to result in a loss of MF-LTP (De Bruyckere et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior published work.

claim: Input-output curves of fEPSP slopes versus axonal fiber volleys revealed no significant differences between control and Bcl11b cKO mice.
source: Under these conditions, input-output curves of fEPSP slopes versus axonal fiber volleys revealed no significant differences between control and Bcl11b cKO mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1a-b; Control +EGFP: 1.95±0.09, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP: 2.02±0.14, mean ± SEM), indicating that basal synaptic transmission was unaltered in the Bcl11b mutants.
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1a-b.

claim: Basal synaptic transmission was unaltered in the Bcl11b mutants.
source: Under these conditions, input-output curves of fEPSP slopes versus axonal fiber volleys revealed no significant differences between control and Bcl11b cKO mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1a-b; Control +EGFP: 1.95±0.09, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP: 2.02±0.14, mean ± SEM), indicating that basal synaptic transmission was unaltered in the Bcl11b mutants.
evidence: This is an inference based on the electrophysiological data showing no difference in input-output curves.

claim: Bcl11b mutants injected with the control AAV displayed a strong reduction of LTP at 20–30 and 30–40 min after induction compared to controls.
source: Compared to controls, Bcl11b mutants injected with the control AAV displayed a strong reduction of LTP at 20–30 and 30–40 min after induction (Figure 3a–c; 0–10 min: Control +EGFP: 90.4±7.2, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP: 106.1±10.8, 10–20 min: Control +EGFP: 42.7±3.6, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP: 39.5±4.6, 20–30 min: Control +EGFP: 52.5±7.6, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP: 24.8±3.2, 30–40 min: Control +EGFP: 50.1±7.3, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP: 20.3±3.7, mean ± SEM), consistent with our previous data (De Bruyckere et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 3a-c.

claim: The loss of LTP was completely reversed upon the re-expression of C1ql2.
source: The loss of LTP was completely reversed upon the re-expression of C1ql2, with the rescue mice exhibiting comparable LTP to controls at all time intervals (Figure 3a–c; 0–10 min: Control +EGFP: 90.4±7.2, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-C1ql2: 86.5±7.4, 10–20 min: Control +EGFP: 42.7±3.6, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-C1ql2: 49.4±5.9, 20–30 min: Control +EGFP: 52.5±7.6, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-C1ql2: 47.2±5.7, 30–40 min: Control +EGFP: 50.1±7.3, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-C1ql2: 44.9±5.3, mean ± SEM).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 3a-c.

claim: The rescue effect of C1ql2 on LTP was specific to C1ql2 as the overexpression of C1ql3 failed to reverse the Bcl11b cKO phenotype.
source: Importantly, this rescue effect was specific to C1ql2 as the overexpression of C1ql3 failed to reverse the Bcl11b cKO phenotype (Figure 3a–c; 0–10 min: Control +EGFP: 90.4±7.2, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-C1ql3: 104.2±9.9, 10–20 min: Control +EGFP: 42.7±3.6, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-C1ql3: 44.4±5.7, 20–30 min: Control +EGFP: 52.5±7.6, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-C1ql3: 29.0±2.3, 30–40 min: Control +EGFP: 50.1±7.3, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-C1ql3: 22.6±2.4, mean ± SEM).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 3a-c.

claim: MF-LTP is known to be mediated by the second messenger cAMP.
source: MF-LTP is known to be mediated by the second messenger cAMP, which is produced by adenylyl cyclase (AC) in response to Ca2+ influx through voltage-gated Ca2+ channels (Li et al., 2007) and kainate receptors (KAR) (Lauri et al., 2001; Schmitz et al., 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: cAMP is produced by adenylyl cyclase in response to Ca2+ influx through voltage-gated Ca2+ channels.
source: MF-LTP is known to be mediated by the second messenger cAMP, which is produced by adenylyl cyclase (AC) in response to Ca2+ influx through voltage-gated Ca2+ channels (Li et al., 2007) and kainate receptors (KAR) (Lauri et al., 2001; Schmitz et al., 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: cAMP is produced by adenylyl cyclase in response to Ca2+ influx through kainate receptors.
source: MF-LTP is known to be mediated by the second messenger cAMP, which is produced by adenylyl cyclase (AC) in response to Ca2+ influx through voltage-gated Ca2+ channels (Li et al., 2007) and kainate receptors (KAR) (Lauri et al., 2001; Schmitz et al., 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Forskolin-induced LTP in Bcl11b cKO mutants had a significantly lower peak and remained significantly weaker throughout the recording compared to slices from control animals.

claim: The regulation of MF-LTP by Bcl11b involves the cAMP-dependent signaling pathway.

claim: The shRNA-mediated KD resulted in a strong reduction of C1ql2 protein levels.

claim: The shRNA-mediated KD of C1ql2 did not affect the expression of C1ql3.

claim: C1ql2 KD reduced the number of docked vesicles per 100 nm of AZ profile length.
source: Compared to controls, C1ql2 KD was sufficient to reduce the average synapse score to similar levels as observed in Bcl11b cKO (Figure 4e, Figure 4—figure supplement 1c;+shNS-EGFP: 3.38±0.069,+shC1ql2-EGFP: 3.15±0.031, mean ± SEM), as well as the number of docked vesicles per 100 nm of AZ profile length (Figure 4f, Figure 4—figure supplement 1d-e;+shNS-EGFP: 0.48±0.04,+shC1ql2-EGFP: 0.31±0.02, mean ± SEM).

claim: C1ql2 KD did not affect the diameter of the docked vesicles.

evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1f-g.

source: Compared to controls, slices from C1ql2 KD mice exhibited a significant reduction of LTP at 20–30 and 30–40 min time intervals, similarly to Bcl11b cKO animals (Figure 4g–i; 0–10 min:+shNS-EGFP: 105.0±4.0,+shC1ql2-EGFP: 94.3±4.5, 10–20 min:+shNS-EGFP: 56.3±4.5,+shC1ql2-EGFP: 35.1±2.8, 20–30 min:+shNS-EGFP: 50.2±4.5,+shC1ql2-EGFP: 23.4±3.5, 30–40 min:+shNS-EGFP: 44.6±4.3,+shC1ql2-EGFP: 20.1±4.1, mean ± SEM).

claim: C1ql2 KD did not affect basal synaptic transmission.

evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1c-d.

claim: KD of C1ql2 in WT DGN recapitulates major phenotypes observed upon Bcl11b cKO.
source: Thus, KD of C1ql2 in WT DGN recapitulates major phenotypes observed upon Bcl11b cKO, supporting that Bcl11b controls SV recruitment and LTP in hippocampal MFS specifically through C1ql2.
evidence: This is an inference based on the similarity of phenotypes between C1ql2 KD and Bcl11b cKO.

claim: Bcl11b controls SV recruitment and LTP in hippocampal MFS specifically through C1ql2.
source: Thus, KD of C1ql2 in WT DGN recapitulates major phenotypes observed upon Bcl11b cKO, supporting that Bcl11b controls SV recruitment and LTP in hippocampal MFS specifically through C1ql2.
evidence: This is an inference based on the rescue and knockdown experiments.

claim: C1ql2 was previously shown to interact with Nrxn3β containing exon 25b sequences.
source: C1ql2 was previously shown to interact with a particular splice variant of Nrxn3β containing exon 25b sequences, Nrxn3(25b+), which was recombinantly expressed in HEK293 cells (Matsuda et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: HEK293 cells secreting C1ql2 had a significantly larger surface area covered by neuronal Nrxn3α(25b+) in comparison to HEK293 cells secreting myc-tag only.
source: HEK293 cells secreting C1ql2 had a significantly larger surface area covered by neuronal Nrxn3α(25b+) in comparison to HEK293 cells secreting myc-tag only (Figure 5b; myc-C1ql2: 39.97±3.99, myc-tag: 17.29±2.27, mean ± SEM).
evidence: This is supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 5b.

claim: vGlut1 accumulation was significantly increased in GFP-Nrxn3α(25b+)-positive neurons contacting C1ql2-secreting HEK293 cells as compared to C1ql2-negative HEK293 cells.
source: Interestingly, vGlut1 accumulation was significantly increased in GFP-Nrxn3α(25b+)-positive neurons contacting C1ql2-secreting HEK293 cells as compared to C1ql2-negative HEK293 cells (Figure 5d; myc-C1ql2: 40.88±3.25, myc-tag: 24.78±4.99, mean ± SEM).
evidence: This is supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 5d.

claim: Neurons with the conditional triple Nrxn KO showed a significantly lower accumulation of endogenous vGlut1 when contacting the C1ql2-secreting HEK293 cells compared to control neurons.
source: Neurons with the conditional triple Nrxn KO (Nrxn cTKO) showed a significantly lower accumulation of endogenous vGlut1 when contacting the C1ql2-secreting HEK293 cells compared to control neurons.
evidence: This is supported by immunocytochemistry data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Selective reintroduction of the Nrxn3α(25b+) isoform into the Nrxn cTKO neurons was sufficient to normalize vGlut1 accumulation in vitro.
source: Strikingly, selective reintroduction of the Nrxn3α(25b+) isoform into the Nrxn cTKO neurons was sufficient to normalize vGlut1 accumulation in vitro (Figure 5f; inactive Cre: 51.66±5.97, Cre: 27.83±2.83, Cre +Nrxn3α(25b+): 39.23±4.3, mean ± SEM).
evidence: This is supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 5f.

claim: The C1ql2-mediated recruitment of vGlut1-positive SV in hippocampal neurons depends on the presence of Nrxn3α(25b+).
source: Collectively, our data strongly suggest that the C1ql2-mediated recruitment of vGlut1-positive SV in hippocampal neurons depends on the presence of Nrxn3α(25b+).
evidence: This is an inference based on the in vitro co-culture experiments.

claim: A change of lysine262 to glutamic acid in C1ql2 renders a large area underneath the C1ql2-specific calcium and receptor binding loops negative.
source: We analyzed the solvent accessible electrostatic surface properties of the C1ql-domain trimeric structure of C1ql2 (Ressl et al., 2015) (PDB_ID: 4QPY) and found that a change of lysine262 (K262) to glutamic acid renders a large area underneath the C1ql2-specific calcium and receptor binding loops negative (Figure 5g) and hypothesized that this would repel binding to Nrxn3(25b+).
evidence: This is based on structural modeling shown in Figure 5g.

claim: In the presence of C1ql2.K262E, recruitment of Nrxn3α(25b+) was significantly lower compared to WT C1ql2 and indistinguishable from myc-tag control levels.
source: In the presence of C1ql2.K262E, recruitment of Nrxn3α(25b+) was significantly lower compared to WT C1ql2 and indistinguishable from myc-tag control levels (Figure 5a–b; myc-K262E: 18.84±5.15).
evidence: This is supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 5a-b.

claim: The expression of C1ql2.K262E in HEK293 cells was unable to accumulate vGlut1 in contacting neurons expressing GFP-Nrxn3α(25b+).
source: Moreover, the expression of C1ql2.K262E in HEK293 cells was unable to accumulate vGlut1 in contacting neurons expressing GFP-Nrxn3α(25b+) (Figure 5c–d; myc-K262E: 16.9±1.2, mean ± SEM).
evidence: This is supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 5c-d.

claim: The clustering of vGlut1 depends on an intact C1ql2-Nrxn3(25b+) interaction.
source: Together, these results provide in vitro evidence that the clustering of vGlut1 depends on an intact C1ql2-Nrxn3(25b+) interaction and that a single point mutation that creates a negative charge of that surface area underneath the C1ql2-specific calcium and receptor binding loops abolishes this binding activity and, thereby, the regulation of SV clustering.
evidence: This is an inference based on the C1ql2.K262E mutant experiments.

claim: A single point mutation that creates a negative charge of the surface area underneath the C1ql2-specific calcium and receptor binding loops abolishes C1ql2 binding activity to Nrxn3(25b+).
source: Together, these results provide in vitro evidence that the clustering of vGlut1 depends on an intact C1ql2-Nrxn3(25b+) interaction and that a single point mutation that creates a negative charge of that surface area underneath the C1ql2-specific calcium and receptor binding loops abolishes this binding activity and, thereby, the regulation of SV clustering.
evidence: This is an inference based on the C1ql2.K262E mutant experiments.

claim: Nrxn3 mRNA levels remain unaltered in Bcl11b cKO.
source: AAV-mediated introduction of C1ql2.K262E in Bcl11b cKO DGN resulted in strong overall expression of the mutant protein (Figure 6b–c; Control +EGFP: 1±0.42, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-K262E: 9.68±4.75, mean ± SEM). However, the spatial distribution of C1ql2.K262E was notably different from the WT protein in the SL of CA3 where most of the MFS are located (Figure 6d). In the SL of CA3, protein levels of C1ql2.K262E were significantly lower compared to WT C1ql2 as quantified by the integrated fluorescence density (Figure 6d–e; Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-C1ql2: 9.75±0.57 × 104, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-K262E: 5.89±0.55 × 104, mean ± SEM).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1a.

claim: AAV-mediated introduction of C1ql2.K262E in Bcl11b cKO DGN resulted in strong overall expression of the mutant protein.
source: AAV-mediated introduction of C1ql2.K262E in Bcl11b cKO DGN resulted in strong overall expression of the mutant protein (Figure 6b–c; Control +EGFP: 1±0.42, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-K262E: 9.68±4.75, mean ± SEM).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6b-c.

claim: The spatial distribution of C1ql2.K262E was notably different from the WT protein in the SL of CA3.
source: However, the spatial distribution of C1ql2.K262E was notably different from the WT protein in the SL of CA3 where most of the MFS are located (Figure 6d).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 6d.

claim: In the SL of CA3, protein levels of C1ql2.K262E were significantly lower compared to WT C1ql2.
source: In the SL of CA3, protein levels of C1ql2.K262E were significantly lower compared to WT C1ql2 as quantified by the integrated fluorescence density (Figure 6d–e; Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-C1ql2: 9.75±0.57 × 104, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-K262E: 5.89±0.55 × 104, mean ± SEM).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 6d-e.

claim: C1ql2.K262E did not rescue the SV distribution in Bcl11b cKO.
source: To investigate whether the remaining C1ql2.K262E affected the SV recruitment, we determined if C1ql2.K262E was able to recover the average synapse score in the Bcl11b cKO background, and found that the mutant C1ql2 variant did not rescue the SV distribution (Figure 6f–g, Figure 6—figure supplement 1c; Control +EGFP: 3.44±0.012, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP: 2.96±0.037, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-K262E: 2.87±0.043, mean ± SEM).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 6f-g and Figure 6—figure supplement 1c.

claim: The number of docked vesicles per 100 nm of AZ profile length in the MFB of animals receiving the C1ql2.K262E AAV was significantly lower compared to control animals and similar to that of Bcl11b mutants.
source: Furthermore, the number of docked vesicles per 100 nm of AZ profile length in the MFB of animals receiving the C1ql2.K262E AAV was significantly lower compared to control animals and similar to that of Bcl11b mutants (Figure 6h, Figure 6—figure supplement 1f-g; Control +EGFP: 0.41±0.049, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP: 0.24±0.038, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-K262E: 0.19±0.025, mean ± SEM).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 6h and Figure 6—figure supplement 1f-g.

claim: C1ql2.K262E was able to rescue the loss of MF-LTP observed in Bcl11b cKO.
source: Unexpectedly, however, C1ql2.K262E was able to rescue the loss of MF-LTP observed in Bcl11b cKO (Figure 6—figure supplement 1h-j; 0–10 min: Control +EGFP: 90.4±7.2, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-K262E: 155.8±30.3, 10–20 min: Control +EGFP: 42.7±3.6, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-K262E: 68.7±17.3, 20–30 min: Control +EGFP: 52.5±7.6, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-K262E: 55.9±13.8, 30–40 min: Control +EGFP: 50.1±7.3, Bcl11b cKO +EGFP-2A-K262E: 47.8±9.3, mean ± SEM).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1h-j.

claim: C1ql2 interacts with specific postsynaptic KAR subunits.
source: It has been shown that C1ql2 also interacts with specific postsynaptic KAR subunits (Matsuda et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Both C1ql2 and C1ql2.K262E had GluK2 bound when precipitated.
source: To test whether the C1ql2.K262E variant retained its ability to interact with GluK2, protein extract of HEK293 cells expressing either GluK2-myc-flag/GFP-C1ql2 or GluK2-myc-flag/GFP-C1ql2.K262E was examined by co-immunoprecipitation and revealed that both C1ql2 and C1ql2.K262E had GluK2 bound when precipitated (Figure 6—figure supplement 1k).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1k.

claim: Bcl11b regulates MFS function through divergent C1ql2-dependent downstream signaling pathways.
source: Together, our data suggest that Bcl11b regulates MFS function through divergent C1ql2-dependent downstream signaling pathways: while SV recruitment depends on a direct interaction of C1ql2 with Nrxn3(25b+), C1ql2 appears to regulate MF-LTP through Nrxn3(25b+)-independent mechanisms.
evidence: This is an inference based on the differential effects of C1ql2.K262E on SV recruitment and LTP.

claim: SV recruitment depends on a direct interaction of C1ql2 with Nrxn3(25b+).
source: Together, our data suggest that Bcl11b regulates MFS function through divergent C1ql2-dependent downstream signaling pathways: while SV recruitment depends on a direct interaction of C1ql2 with Nrxn3(25b+), C1ql2 appears to regulate MF-LTP through Nrxn3(25b+)-independent mechanisms.
evidence: This is an inference based on the C1ql2.K262E experiments showing loss of SV recruitment rescue.

claim: C1ql2 appears to regulate MF-LTP through Nrxn3(25b+)-independent mechanisms.
source: Together, our data suggest that Bcl11b regulates MFS function through divergent C1ql2-dependent downstream signaling pathways: while SV recruitment depends on a direct interaction of C1ql2 with Nrxn3(25b+), C1ql2 appears to regulate MF-LTP through Nrxn3(25b+)-independent mechanisms.
evidence: This is an inference based on the C1ql2.K262E experiments showing rescue of LTP despite loss of Nrxn3 binding.

claim: AAV expressing GFP-tagged Cre in Nrxn1, 2 & 3flox/flox mice resulted in strong reduction of Nrxn3 mRNA levels in DGN.
source: To further explore whether binding to Nrxn3 is required for C1ql2-dependent regulation of SV recruitment, we stereotaxically injected an AAV expressing GFP-tagged Cre or inactive Cre into the DG of 2-month-old Nrxn1, 2 & 3flox/flox mice (Figure 7a), which resulted in strong reduction of Nrxn3 mRNA levels in DGN 2 months later.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Fluorescence intensity of endogenous C1ql2 protein along the MF axons in the SL of CA3 was significantly reduced in Nrxn cTKO animals compared to controls.
source: Fluorescence intensity of endogenous C1ql2 protein along the MF axons in the SL of CA3 was significantly reduced in Nrxn cTKO animals compared to Nrxn1, 2 & 3flox/flox animals expressing inactive Cre (Figure 7c–d;+inactive Cre: 11.72±1.63,+Cre: 4.71±0.93, mean ± SEM).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 7c-d.

claim: C1ql2 mRNA levels in DGN remained unchanged in Nrxn cTKO.
source: However, C1ql2 mRNA levels in DGN remained unchanged (Figure 7—figure supplement 1b;+inactive Cre: 1±0.23,+Cre: 0.8±0.11, mean ± SEM), suggesting that overall production of C1ql2 protein was not affected.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1b.

claim: Overall production of C1ql2 protein was not affected in Nrxn cTKO.
source: However, C1ql2 mRNA levels in DGN remained unchanged (Figure 7—figure supplement 1b;+inactive Cre: 1±0.23,+Cre: 0.8±0.11, mean ± SEM), suggesting that overall production of C1ql2 protein was not affected.
evidence: This is an inference based on the unchanged C1ql2 mRNA levels.

claim: ZnT3 levels remained unchanged in Nrxn cTKO compared to controls.
source: To exclude that the reduced C1ql2 fluorescence intensity was simply a consequence of an overall loss of MFB, we used ZnT3 as a marker of MFB and found it unchanged in Nrxn cTKO compared to controls (Figure 7e).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 7e.

claim: Disruption of the C1ql2-Nrxn3(25b+) binding by ablation of Nrxn3 in Nrxn cTKO mutants recapitulated the phenotype observed upon Bcl11b ablation or by KD of C1ql2.
source: Remarkably, disruption of the C1ql2-Nrxn3(25b+) binding by ablation of Nrxn3 in Nrxn cTKO mutants not only led to reduced C1ql2 fluorescence intensity (Figure 7c–d), but recapitulated the phenotype observed upon Bcl11b ablation or by KD of C1ql2 as evidenced by a large reduction of the average synapse score in Nrxn cTKO (Figure 7f–g, Figure 7—figure supplement 1d;+inactive Cre: 3.11±0.06;+Cre: 2.67±0.074, mean ± SEM).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 7f-g and Figure 7—figure supplement 1d.

claim: The number of docked vesicles per 100 nm of AZ profile length in Nrxn cTKO was diminished compared to controls.
source: Also, similarly to the Bcl11b and C1ql2 mutant phenotypes, we observed the number of docked vesicles per 100 nm of AZ profile length in Nrxn cTKO to be diminished compared to controls (Figure 7h, Figure 7—figure supplement 1e-f;+inactive Cre: 0.404±0.035,+Cre: 0.195±0.02, mean ± SEM), whereas the AZ length and the diameter of docked vesicles remained unchanged (Figure 7—figure supplement 1g-h; AZ length:+inactive Cre: 193.2±6.88;+Cre: 188.44±11.43, mean ± SEM; Vesicle diameter:+inactive Cre: 38.38±0.44;+Cre: 37.12±0.8, mean ± SEM).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 7h and Figure 7—figure supplement 1e-f.

claim: Bcl11b controls MFS organization through C1ql2/Nrxn3(25b+)-dependent signaling.
source: Thus, our results provide evidence that Bcl11b controls MFS organization through C1ql2/Nrxn3(25b+)-dependent signaling, explicating how Bcl11b, a transcription factor with a broad range of functions, can regulate highly specific processes in the brain.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combined results of the study.

claim: Bcl11b is involved in the pathogenesis of neurodevelopmental as well as neuropsychiatric disorders that are frequently associated with synaptic dysfunction.

evidence: This statement is supported by citations in the introduction and discussion sections.

claim: Bcl11b is essential for synapse function in the mossy fiber circuit of the adult murine hippocampus.

evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: C1ql2 has been associated with neuropsychiatric disorders.
source: Recent studies suggested Nrxn3, as well as C1ql2, to be associated with neuropsychiatric disorders (Hishimoto et al., 2007; Hu et al., 2013; Huggett and Stallings, 2020a; Marballi et al., 2022).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: This study identifies a Bcl11b/C1ql2/Nrxn3-dependent signaling pathway in the control of basic structural and functional properties of MFS.

evidence: This is a summary statement of the main findings of the study.

claim: MF-LTP manifests as a long-term increase in presynaptic vesicle release probability.

evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: MF-LTP directly depends on the distribution of SV in the proximity of the AZ.
source: MF-LTP, which manifests as a long-term increase in presynaptic vesicle release probability (Pr) (Shahoha et al., 2022), directly depends on the distribution of SV in the proximity of the AZ.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge and inference from cited literature.

claim: The increase in Pr involves the recruitment of new AZ and an increase in the number of docked and tethered vesicles.
source: Recent studies have shown that the increase in Pr involves the recruitment of new AZ and an increase in the number of docked and tethered vesicles, corresponding to the readily releasable pool of SV (Orlando et al., 2021; Vandael et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The perturbed SV recruitment in both Bcl11b cKO and C1ql2 KD mice could potentially explain the loss of LTP in both conditions.
source: The perturbed SV recruitment in both Bcl11b cKO and C1ql2 KD mice could thus potentially explain the loss of LTP in both conditions.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the observed correlation between SV recruitment and LTP.

source: Additional factors have been suggested to contribute to the increase in Pr, including a tighter coupling between Ca2+ channels and SV (Midorikawa and Sakaba, 2017) and the accumulation of Ca2+ channels near release sites (Fukaya et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Additional factors have been suggested to contribute to the increase in Pr, including the accumulation of Ca2+ channels near release sites.
source: Additional factors have been suggested to contribute to the increase in Pr, including a tighter coupling between Ca2+ channels and SV (Midorikawa and Sakaba, 2017) and the accumulation of Ca2+ channels near release sites (Fukaya et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The loss of LTP in Bcl11b cKO is caused by a process downstream of the initial presynaptic Ca2+ influx following stimulation.
source: By using forskolin to directly activate AC, we bypassed these initial steps, and still found a reduction of LTP in Bcl11b cKO mice, similarly to HFS. These results strongly suggest that the loss of LTP is caused by a process downstream of the initial presynaptic Ca2+ influx following stimulation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the forskolin experiment.

claim: C1ql proteins are complement-related factors that are synthesized by the presynapse and secreted into the synaptic cleft.
source: C1ql proteins are complement-related factors that are synthesized by the presynapse and secreted into the synaptic cleft.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about C1ql proteins.

claim: Within the hippocampus, C1ql2 and –3 protein expression overlaps and is highly restricted to DGN.
source: Within the hippocampus, C1ql2 and –3 protein expression overlaps and is highly restricted to DGN (Iijima et al., 2010) and the corresponding mossy fiber system, including MF-CA3 synapses.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: C1ql2 and –3 were previously suggested to form functional heteromers that can cluster postsynaptic KAR on MFS.
source: C1ql2 and –3 were previously suggested to form functional heteromers that can cluster postsynaptic KAR on MFS.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Selective deletion of either C1ql2 or –3 in mice was reported to have no overt mutant hippocampal phenotype.
source: Selective deletion of either C1ql2 or –3 in mice was reported to have no overt mutant hippocampal phenotype, suggesting functional compensation for both proteins (Matsuda et al., 2016).
